prefix:
The Racial Geography of the Federal Death Penalty
Scholars have devoted substantial attention
text:
to the geography of the federal death penalty, both theoretically and empirically. One strand of this research interest focused on understanding what we know about the geography of the federal death penalty, and what we don’t know about the geography of the other crimes, crimes involving racial and ethnic minorities. In this paper, we review the knowledge of the space and distribution of federal death penalty cases. While we focus primarily on the national level, many scholar groups also have addressed the global scale level—application to our own communities and crime investigations. We assembled research data from a study applying statistics and feminist theory in this empirical analysis.

Many teachers remain home during the day while computers remain inside the classroom. Even if you have a computer class, imagine the chaos that would ensue if you had to work at a Computer while teaching online. Does that make for tight-paced, intense classrooms?
Remember, a teacher is not just an instructor of online learning. A classroom teacher is not a computer teacher. A classroom teacher is not an interactive speaker. prefix: A new study conducted by researchers at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and
text:
the State University of New York at Morrisville, has demonstrated that even though lakes can be contaminated during the ice season, many people, especially people of Michigan or Northeastern Ontario, can still swim in them in summer.
The study, which was conducted eight years ago and published this week in Aquatic Biodiversity, is the first to evaluate the effects of climate change on lakes and their biodiversity and life forms, as well as the impacts to native flora even in lakes that have not changed. The findings showed that lakes that have been in some way affected by climate change can be contaminated by ice.
Ice represents one of the largest sources of contaminants in lakes today, and ranges from soft snow to frozen mud, depending on the season. It is estimated that the United States has 84 ice-covered areas in office, and those areas may reach up to 1.5 meters (63 feet) above sea level (ASL) if they were solely ice-covered. Aquatic Biodiversity chronicled the effects of moderate andices on lake species and communities during the 2007 and 2008 ice melts.

prefix: Hincks Wilderness Protection Area is a protected area in the Australian state of South Australia
text:
. It is one of the largest protected areas in the Southern Hemisphere, covering 110.7 km2 in areas in the Mid-South Region (Mechelbach River drainage).

Features
An entry on the Lock Allan Steypool  makes reference to the protected area by saying "Gelimbil expects visitors to secure a camera".

The name Hincks has been widely known in Australia and internationally, with Hincks Point, the party's base. Geology and reef environments have been found at a variety of sites within parks across the state, includingYeitchvic Creek on the Fitzroy Peninsula, East Mallee River areas, reef on the Coolangatta breakwater, and Onslow Shoals on Eyre Peninsula. These reef environments are typical for the ecologically important Barrier Cut and included in the National Park Inventory.

The parks and reefs are complimented by a wealth of marine and freshwater habitats. These are maintained through a wealth of conservation land management committed to protecting and preserving habitats, especially by maintaining healthy ecological communities and healthy tidal creeks. Marine reserves are key parts of the landscape, providing bare-grave foraging habitat, warm water moulting habitat, stable waters for fish to spawn and estuary rehabilitation to promote sustainable fisheries.
